ESV.1: “Now this is the commandment — the statutes and the rules  — that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, that you may do them in the land to which you are going over, to possess it,
ESV.2: that you may fear the LORD your God, you and your son and your son's son, by keeping all his statutes and his commandments, which I command you, all the days of your life, and that your days may be long.
ESV.3: Hear therefore, O Israel, and be careful to do them, that it may go well with you, and that you may multiply greatly, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
ESV.4: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
ESV.5: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
ESV.6: And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart.
ESV.7: You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
ESV.8: You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
ESV.9: You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
ESV.10: “And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give you — with great and good cities that you did not build,
ESV.11: and houses full of all good things that you did not fill, and cisterns that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant — and when you eat and are full,
ESV.12: then take care lest you forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
ESV.13: It is the LORD your God you shall fear. Him you shall serve and by his name you shall swear.
ESV.14: You shall not go after other gods, the gods of the peoples who are around you —
ESV.15: for the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God — lest the anger of the LORD your God be kindled against you, and he destroy you from off the face of the earth.
ESV.16: “You shall not put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested him at Massah.
ESV.17: You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and his testimonies and his statutes, which he has commanded you.
ESV.18: And you shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, that it may go well with you, and that you may go in and take possession of the good land that the LORD swore to give to your fathers
ESV.19: by thrusting out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has promised.
ESV.20: “When your son asks you in time to come, ‘What is the meaning of the testimonies and the statutes and the rules that the LORD our God has commanded you?’
ESV.21: then you shall say to your son, ‘We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt. And the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
ESV.22: And the LORD showed signs and wonders, great and grievous, against Egypt and against Pharaoh and all his household, before our eyes.
ESV.23: And he brought us out from there, that he might bring us in and give us the land that he swore to give to our fathers.
ESV.24: And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as we are this day.
ESV.25: And it will be righteousness for us, if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us.’

NKJV.1: “Now this is the commandment, and these are the statutes and judgments which the LORD your God has commanded to teach you, that you may observe them in the land which you are crossing over to possess,
NKJV.2: that you may fear the LORD your God, to keep all His statutes and His commandments which I command you, you and your son and your grandson, all the days of your life, and that your days may be prolonged.
NKJV.3: Therefore hear, O Israel, and be careful to observe it, that it may be well with you, and that you may multiply greatly as the LORD God of your fathers has promised you— ‘a land flowing with milk and honey.’
NKJV.4: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one!
NKJV.5: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
NKJV.6: “And these words which I command you today shall be in your heart.
NKJV.7: You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up.
NKJV.8: You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
NKJV.9: You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
NKJV.10: “So it shall be, when the LORD your God brings you into the land of which He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you large and beautiful cities which you did not build,
NKJV.11: houses full of all good things, which you did not fill, hewn-out wells which you did not dig, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant— when you have eaten and are full—
NKJV.12: then beware, lest you forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
NKJV.13: You shall fear the LORD your God and serve Him, and shall take oaths in His name.
NKJV.14: You shall not go after other gods, the gods of the peoples who are all around you
NKJV.15: (for the LORD your God is a jealous God among you), lest the anger of the LORD your God be aroused against you and destroy you from the face of the earth.
NKJV.16: “You shall not tempt the LORD your God as you tempted Him in Massah.
NKJV.17: You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, His testimonies, and His statutes which He has commanded you.
NKJV.18: And you shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, that it may be well with you, and that you may go in and possess the good land of which the LORD swore to your fathers,
NKJV.19: to cast out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.
NKJV.20: “When your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is the meaning of the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which the LORD our God has commanded you?’
NKJV.21: then you shall say to your son: ‘We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand;
NKJV.22: and the LORD showed signs and wonders before our eyes, great and severe, against Egypt, Pharaoh, and all his household.
NKJV.23: Then He brought us out from there, that He might bring us in, to give us the land of which He swore to our fathers.
NKJV.24: And the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that He might preserve us alive, as it is this day.
NKJV.25: Then it will be righteousness for us, if we are careful to observe all these commandments before the LORD our God, as He has commanded us.’

NASB.1: 'Now this is the commandment, the statutes and the judgments which the LORD your God has commanded [me] to teach you, that you might do [them] in the land where you are going over to possess it,
NASB.2: so that you and your son and your grandson might fear the LORD your God, to keep all His statutes and His commandments which I command you, all the days of your life, and that your days may be prolonged.
NASB.3: 'O Israel, you should listen and be careful to do [it], that it may be well with you and that you may multiply greatly, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you, [in] a land flowing with milk and honey.
NASB.4: 'Hear, O Israel! The LORD is our God, the LORD is one!
NASB.5: 'You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
NASB.6: 'These words, which I am commanding you today, shall be on your heart.
NASB.7: You shall teach them diligently to your sons and shall talk of them when you sit in your house and when you walk by the way and when you lie down and when you rise up.
NASB.8: 'You shall bind them as a sign on your hand and they shall be as frontals on your forehead.
NASB.9: 'You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
NASB.10: 'Then it shall come about when the LORD your God brings you into the land which He swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to give you, great and splendid cities which you did not build,
NASB.11: and houses full of all good things which you did not fill, and hewn cisterns which you did not dig, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you eat and are satisfied,
NASB.12: then watch yourself, that you do not forget the LORD who brought you from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
NASB.13: 'You shall fear [only] the LORD your God; and you shall worship Him and swear by His name.
NASB.14: 'You shall not follow other gods, any of the gods of the peoples who surround you,
NASB.15: for the LORD your God in the midst of you is a jealous God; otherwise the anger of the LORD your God will be kindled against you, and He will wipe you off the face of the earth.
NASB.16: 'You shall not put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested [Him] at Massah.
NASB.17: 'You should diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes which He has commanded you.
NASB.18: 'You shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, that it may be well with you and that you may go in and possess the good land which the LORD swore to [give] your fathers,
NASB.19: by driving out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.
NASB.20: 'When your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What [do] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments [mean] which the LORD our God commanded you?'
NASB.21: then you shall say to your son, 'We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us from Egypt with a mighty hand.
NASB.22: 'Moreover, the LORD showed great and distressing signs and wonders before our eyes against Egypt, Pharaoh and all his household;
NASB.23: He brought us out from there in order to bring us in, to give us the land which He had sworn to our fathers.'
NASB.24: 'So the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God for our good always and for our survival, as [it is] today.
NASB.25: 'It will be righteousness for us if we are careful to observe all this commandment before the LORD our God, just as He commanded us.

WEB.1: Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which Yahweh your God commanded to teach you, that you might do them in the land where you go over to possess it;
WEB.2: that you might fear Yahweh your God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments, which I command you; you, and your son, and your son’s son, all the days of your life; and that your days may be prolonged.
WEB.3: Hear therefore, Israel, and observe to do it; that it may be well with you, and that you may increase mightily, as Yahweh, the God of your fathers, has promised to you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
WEB.4: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one.
WEB.5: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
WEB.6: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart;
WEB.7: and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
WEB.8: You shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.
WEB.9: You shall write them on the door posts of your house, and on your gates.
WEB.10: It shall be, when Yahweh your God brings you into the land which he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give you, great and goodly cities, which you didn’t build,
WEB.11: and houses full of all good things, which you didn’t fill, and cisterns dug out, which you didn’t dig, vineyards and olive trees, which you didn’t plant, and you shall eat and be full;
WEB.12: then beware lest you forget Yahweh, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
WEB.13: You shall fear Yahweh your God; and you shall serve him, and shall swear by his name.
WEB.14: You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples who are around you;
WEB.15: for Yahweh your God among you is a jealous God; lest the anger of Yahweh your God be kindled against you, and he destroy you from off the face of the earth.
WEB.16: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.
WEB.17: You shall diligently keep the commandments of Yahweh your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he has commanded you.
WEB.18: You shall do that which is right and good in Yahweh’s sight; that it may be well with you, and that you may go in and possess the good land which Yahweh swore to your fathers,
WEB.19: to thrust out all your enemies from before you, as Yahweh has spoken.
WEB.20: When your son asks you in time to come, saying, “What do the testimonies, the statutes, and the ordinances, which Yahweh our God has commanded you mean?”
WEB.21: then you shall tell your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt. Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand;
WEB.22: and Yahweh showed great and awesome signs and wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on all his house, before our eyes;
WEB.23: and he brought us out from there, that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he swore to our fathers.
WEB.24: Yahweh commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Yahweh our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as we are today.
WEB.25: It shall be righteousness to us, if we observe to do all this commandment before Yahweh our God, as he has commanded us.”

CSB17.1: “This is the command — the statutes and ordinances — the LORD your God has commanded me to teach you, so that you may follow them in the land you are about to enter and possess. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.2: Do this so that you may fear <sup>ⓚ</sup> the LORD your God <sup>ⓛ</sup> all the days of your life <sup>ⓜ</sup> by keeping all his statutes and commands I am giving you, your son, and your grandson, and so that you may have a long life. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.3: Listen, Israel, and be careful to follow them, so that you may prosper and multiply greatly, because the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you a land flowing with milk and honey. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.4: “Listen, Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one. <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.5: Love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.6: These words that I am giving you today are to be in your heart. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.7: Repeat them to your children. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Talk about them when you sit in your house and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
CSB17.8: Bind them as a sign on your hand and let them be a symbol <sup>[2]</sup> on your forehead. <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.9: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your city gates.
CSB17.10: “When the LORD your God brings you into the land he swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you — a land with large and beautiful cities that you did not build,
CSB17.11: houses full of every good thing that you did not fill them with, cisterns that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant <sup>ⓖ</sup>  — and when you eat and are satisfied, <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.12: be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.13: Fear the LORD your God, worship him, and take your oaths in his name. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.14: Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you,
CSB17.15: for the LORD your God, who is among you, is a jealous God. <sup>ⓚ</sup> Otherwise, the LORD your God will become angry with you and obliterate you from the face of the earth.
CSB17.16: Do not test <sup>ⓛ</sup> the LORD your God as you tested him at Massah. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.17: Carefully observe the commands of the LORD your God, the decrees and statutes he has commanded you.
CSB17.18: Do what is right and good in the LORD’s sight, so that you may prosper and so that you may enter and possess the good land <sup>ⓝ</sup> the LORD your God swore to give your fathers, <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.19: by driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.20: “When your son asks you in the future, ‘What is the meaning <sup>ⓒ</sup> of the decrees, statutes, and ordinances that the LORD our God has commanded you?’
CSB17.21: tell him, ‘We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.22: Before our eyes the LORD inflicted great and devastating signs and wonders on Egypt, <sup>ⓔ</sup> on Pharaoh, and on all his household,
CSB17.23: but he brought us from there in order to lead us in and give us the land that he swore to our fathers.
CSB17.24: The LORD commanded us to follow all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God for our prosperity always and for our preservation, as it is today.
CSB17.25: Righteousness will be ours if we are careful to follow every one of these commands before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us.’

NLT.1: “These are the commands, decrees, and regulations that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you. You must obey them in the land you are about to enter and occupy,
NLT.2: and you and your children and grandchildren must fear the LORD your God as long as you live. If you obey all his decrees and commands, you will enjoy a long life.
NLT.3: Listen closely, Israel, and be careful to obey. Then all will go well with you, and you will have many children in the land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
NLT.4: “Listen, O Israel! The LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
NLT.5: And you must love the LORD your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.
NLT.6: And you must commit yourselves wholeheartedly to these commands that I am giving you today.
NLT.7: Repeat them again and again to your children. Talk about them when you are at home and when you are on the road, when you are going to bed and when you are getting up.
NLT.8: Tie them to your hands and wear them on your forehead as reminders.
NLT.9: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
NLT.10: “The LORD your God will soon bring you into the land he swore to give you when he made a vow to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is a land with large, prosperous cities that you did not build.
NLT.11: The houses will be richly stocked with goods you did not produce. You will draw water from cisterns you did not dig, and you will eat from vineyards and olive trees you did not plant. When you have eaten your fill in this land,
NLT.12: be careful not to forget the LORD, who rescued you from slavery in the land of Egypt.
NLT.13: You must fear the LORD your God and serve him. When you take an oath, you must use only his name.
NLT.14: “You must not worship any of the gods of neighboring nations,

AMP.1: "Now this is the command; the statutes and the judgments (precepts) which the LORD your God has commanded me to teach you, so that you might do (follow, obey) them in the land which you are crossing over [the Jordan] to possess,
AMP.2: so that you and your son and your grandson may fear and worship the LORD your God [with awe-filled reverence and profound respect], to keep [and actively do] all His statutes and His commandments which I am commanding you, all the days of your life, so that your days may be prolonged.
AMP.3: Therefore listen, O Israel, and be careful to do them, that it may go well with you and that you may increase greatly [in numbers], as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
AMP.4: "Hear, O Israel! The LORD is our God, the LORD is one [the only God]!
AMP.5: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and mind and with all your soul and with all your strength [your entire being].
AMP.6: These words, which I am commanding you today, shall be [written] on your heart and mind.
AMP.7: You shall teach them diligently to your children [impressing God's precepts on their minds and penetrating their hearts with His truths] and shall speak of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road and when you lie down and when you get up.
AMP.8: And you shall bind them as a sign on your hand (forearm), and they shall be used as bands (frontals, frontlets) on your forehead.
AMP.9: You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
AMP.10: "Then it shall come about when the LORD your God brings you into the land which He swore (solemnly promised) to [give] your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—to give you, [a land with] great and splendid cities which you did not build,
AMP.11: and houses full of all good things which you did not fill, and hewn (excavated) cisterns (wells) which you did not dig out, and vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you eat and are full and satisfied,
AMP.12: then beware that you do not forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
AMP.13: You shall fear [only] the LORD your God; and you shall serve Him [with awe-filled reverence and profound respect] and swear [oaths] by His name [alone].
AMP.14: You shall not follow other gods, any of the gods of the peoples who surround you,
AMP.15: for the LORD your God who is among you is a jealous (impassioned) God [demanding what is rightfully and uniquely His]—otherwise the anger of the LORD your God will be kindled and burn against you, and He will destroy you from the face of the earth.
AMP.16: "You shall not put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested Him at Massah.
AMP.17: You shall diligently keep [foremost in your thoughts and actively do] the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes which He has commanded you.
AMP.18: You shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, so that it may be well with you and that you may go in and possess the good land which the LORD swore to [give] your fathers,
AMP.19: by driving out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.
AMP.20: "When your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What is the meaning of the testimonies and statutes and judgments (precepts) which the LORD our God has commanded you?'
AMP.21: then you shall say to your son, 'We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
AMP.22: Moreover, the LORD showed great and terrible signs and wonders before our eyes against Egypt, Pharaoh and all his household;
AMP.23: He brought us out from there in order to bring us in, to give us the land which He had sworn to [give] our fathers.'
AMP.24: So the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear [and worship] the LORD our God [with awe-filled reverence and profound respect] for our good always and so that He might preserve us alive, as it is today.
AMP.25: It will be [considered] righteousness for us [that is, right standing with God] if we are careful to observe all this commandment before the LORD our God—just as He has commanded us.

MSG.1: This is the commandment, the rules and regulations, that God, your God, commanded me to teach you to live out in the land you're about to cross into to possess.
MSG.2: This is so that you'll live in deep reverence before God lifelong, observing all his rules and regulations that I'm commanding you, you and your children and your grandchildren, living good long lives.
MSG.3: Listen obediently, Israel. Do what you're told so that you'll have a good life, a life of abundance and bounty, just as God promised, in a land abounding in milk and honey.
MSG.4:
Attention, Israel!
God, our God! God the one and only!
MSG.5: Love God, your God, with your whole heart: love him with all that's in you, love him with all you've got!
MSG.6: Write these commandments that I've given you today on your hearts. Get them inside of you
MSG.7: and then get them inside your children. Talk about them wherever you are, sitting at home or walking in the street; talk about them from the time you get up in the morning to when you fall into bed at night.
MSG.8: Tie them on your hands and foreheads as a reminder;
MSG.9: inscribe them on the doorposts of your homes and on your city gates.
MSG.10: When God, your God, ushers you into the land he promised through your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give you, you're going to walk into large, bustling cities you didn't build,
MSG.11: well-furnished houses you didn't buy, come upon wells you didn't dig, vineyards and olive orchards you didn't plant. When you take it all in and settle down, pleased and content,
MSG.12: make sure you don't forget how you got there—God brought you out of slavery in Egypt.
MSG.13: Deeply respect God, your God. Serve and worship him exclusively. Back up your promises with his name only.
MSG.14: Don't fool around with other gods, the gods of your neighbors,
MSG.15: because God, your God, who is alive among you is a jealous God. Don't provoke him, igniting his hot anger that would burn you right off the face of the Earth.
MSG.16: Don't push God, your God, to the wall as you did that day at Massah, the Testing-Place.
MSG.17: Carefully keep the commands of God, your God, all the requirements and regulations he gave you.
MSG.18: Do what is right; do what is good in God's sight so you'll live a good life and be able to march in and take this pleasant land that God so solemnly promised through your ancestors,
MSG.19: throwing out your enemies left and right—exactly as God said.
MSG.20: The next time your child asks you, "What do these requirements and regulations and rules that God, our God, has commanded mean?"
MSG.21: tell your child, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt and God powerfully intervened and got us out of that country.
MSG.22: We stood there and watched as God delivered miracle-signs, great wonders, and evil-visitations on Egypt, on Pharaoh and his household.
MSG.23: He pulled us out of there so he could bring us here and give us the land he so solemnly promised to our ancestors.
MSG.24: That's why God commanded us to follow all these rules, so that we would live reverently before God, our God, as he gives us this good life, keeping us alive for a long time to come.
MSG.25: "It will be a set-right and put-together life for us if we make sure that we do this entire commandment in the Presence of God, our God, just as he commanded us to do."
